analysis.title: 2027 US macro outlook teaser: a modest slowdown but still relatively resilient as Fed hikes further
key_insights: CACIB tracks 2026 US growth at 2.3% on an annual average basis, matching 2025 and above its 2.1% start-of-year expectation despite the Iran war.
Forecast is growth of 2.1% in 2027 and 2.0% in 2028. On a Q4/Q4 basis growth slows from 2.5% to 1.9%.

Support pillars are strong household balance sheets, the AI investment boom, and lower interest rate sensitivity. Growth is concentrated, so a further correction in AI-linked equities is a clear downside risk.

Labour market has stabilised after cooling in late 2025. NFP averaged +74k over 12 months vs +191k pre-Covid, but lower immigration cut the breakeven, so unemployment is seen in the low-4% range (4.2% in the table).
Headline CPI is seen above 3% into Q127, briefly dipping below 2% on base effects, then stabilising near 2.3%. Core holds near 2.8% through Q127 and eases to 2.4-2.5% by end-2027.

Fed call: 25bp hikes in December 2026 and March 2027, pausing with the upper bound at 4.50%. Risks are tilted to the upside, including hikes at consecutive meetings (December, January, March to 4.75%) or a higher terminal rate.
Easing is penciled in later: 25bp cuts in Q427 and Q128 take the upper bound to 4.00%. Inflation still above target and a higher neutral rate limit easing.
CACIB is more dovish than the market, which prices just over three hikes vs CACIB's two. Market pricing may win if inflation does not improve by mid-2027.

Policy assumptions: a Democratic Congress facing the filibuster and Trump's veto implies gridlock, stable deficit, and less fiscal impulse in 2027 vs OBBBA in 2026. Tariffs and immigration are seen at status quo.

AI investment may slow from 2026's pace (nonresidential investment rose over 10% on average in the first three quarters of 2026). Hyperscalers pledge over USD1trn in 2027. State-level AI regulation may slow or relocate projects.
Financial wealth effect is estimated at USD0.02-0.03 per USD1.00 change, so an equity correction would be a material headwind but not a cliff.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Tracking slightly above the 2.1% start-of-year expectation, showing resilience.
Slowdown is more visible on Q4/Q4 basis.

macro_indicators.reading: about 2.3% by late 2027, briefly below 2% on base effects
macro_indicators.interpretation: Inflation eases after sticky near term.
Low-hire, low-fire keeps labour market balanced.

macro_indicators.reading: 4.50% peak after hikes in Dec 2026 and Mar 2027, 4.00% by Q128
macro_indicators.interpretation: Further tightening then modest easing, hawkish risk skew.
Slow hiring but lower breakeven from immigration policy.

risk_factors: Further correction in AI-related equities causing investment pullback and negative wealth effect.
AI investment growth cannot sustain 2026 pace, and regulation may shift.
Second-round inflation effects from Iran war energy surge could be larger, prompting more or faster Fed hikes.
Concentrated growth in AI investment and upper-income households.
charts_described: Fig 1 table forecasts 2027 GDP 2.1%, CPI 2.4% annual average, core CPI 2.7%, unemployment 4.2%, and fed funds upper bound 4.25% annual average.
Fig 4 plots NFP 3-mo MA, private NFP 3-mo MA and the Dallas Fed smoothed breakeven estimate, which has dropped sharply.
Fig 6 compares CACIB effective Fed funds forecast with market pricing as of 17 Nov and September dot plot median, showing market pricing just over three hikes vs CACIB's two.
vol_and_positioning: Market prices just over three Fed hikes vs CACIB's two (pricing as of 17 Nov).
geopolitical: Iran war drove energy costs and inflation. Base case has no major military re-escalation, though Trump's tone has been more conciliatory after elections and re-escalation risk remains.
Democrats will push to wind down the Iran war but presidential foreign policy powers complicate it.
Tariffs and immigration can be changed by Trump without Congress. Weighted average tariff rate expected roughly steady.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong household balance sheets, AI investment above USD1trn pledged in 2027, and low rate sensitivity support 2.1% growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth is concentrated in AI investment and upper-income households. An AI equity correction would cut investment and hit wealth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further correction in AI-linked equities, or AI investment slowing sharply from the over 10% pace of 2026.

theme_stances.key_argument: Sticky near-term inflation and stable labour market lead to hikes in December 2026 and March 2027, with upside risks.
theme_stances.evidence: we see risks as tilted to the upside

theme_stances.key_argument: AI investment and household balance sheets keep growth solid, though concentration creates vulnerability.
theme_stances.evidence: the relatively concentrated nature of growth does create some vulnerability
